data.name: Air Fryer Salmon
data.description: Tender salmon fillets develop lightly browned edges beneath a fragrant coating of lemon zest, garlic and black pepper. Fresh lemon juice adds a bright finish to the rich, flaky fish.

refrigerator.notes: Refrigerate leftovers in a shallow, covered container within 2 hours of cooking, or within 1 hour when the surrounding temperature exceeds 32°C (90°F). Store at 4°C (40°F) or below.

freezer.notes: Freeze cooled portions in an airtight freezer container at -18°C (0°F) or below for best quality. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator.

storage.reheating: Air-fry refrigerated portions at 160°C (320°F), checking after 4 minutes and continuing until the center reaches 74°C (165°F). Reheated salmon may be firmer than freshly cooked salmon.

equipment.name: Air fryer with a basket large enough for two separated fillets

items.name: salmon fillets
items.notes: Two fillets weighing 180 g each, approximately 2.5 cm thick. Weight is edible flesh after skin and bones are removed.

items.name: garlic
items.notes: Weigh after removing the papery skin.

items.name: lemon zest
items.notes: Use only the yellow outer peel of a washed lemon, avoiding the bitter white pith.

instructions.text: Preheat the air fryer to 200°C (392°F) for 3 minutes.
Pat the salmon thoroughly dry with paper towels on the preparation plate.
tips: Do not rinse raw fish. Wash hands with soap and water after handling it, and clean surfaces and utensils that touch it. Keep the serving plates separate from the raw-fish preparation plate.

instructions.text: Mix the olive oil, garlic, lemon zest, salt and black pepper in the small bowl with the spoon.
Spread all the seasoning mixture thinly over the tops, sides and undersides of both salmon fillets using the spoon.
tips: Keep the garlic in a thin, even layer so protruding pieces do not scorch.

instructions.text: Arrange the fillets in the air-fryer basket with their flatter sides down and at least 2 cm of space between them.

Air-fry at 200°C (392°F) for approximately 8–12 minutes without flipping. Begin checking at 8 minutes with the instant-read thermometer inserted sideways into the thickest part of each fillet. Continue cooking until both centers reach 63°C (145°F); the edges should be lightly browned and the flesh should separate into moist flakes.

doneness_cues.visual: Lightly browned edges and opaque flesh that separates into flakes.
doneness_cues.tactile: The center yields gently and separates under light pressure.

tips: Temperature determines doneness; thickness and air-fryer performance can change the cooking time.

The minimum temperature for fish is 63°C (145°F), and reheated leftovers must reach 74°C (165°F). [FoodSafety.gov temperature guidance](https://www.foodsafety.gov/food-safety-charts/safe-minimum-internal-temperatures).

instructions.text: Transfer the cooked fillets to clean serving plates with a clean fish spatula.
Drizzle the lemon juice evenly over both portions just before serving.

troubleshooting.symptom: The salmon is dry or chalky.
troubleshooting.likely_cause: The fillets cooked beyond the required temperature, or one fillet was substantially thinner than the other.
troubleshooting.prevention: Choose similarly thick portions and begin checking their centers at 8 minutes. Remove each fillet once it reaches 63°C (145°F).
troubleshooting.fix: Lost moisture cannot be restored. Flake the salmon and distribute the lemon finish over it to improve eating quality.

troubleshooting.symptom: The garlic darkens before the salmon is cooked through.
troubleshooting.likely_cause: Garlic was left in coarse pieces or piled thickly on the surface.
troubleshooting.prevention: Finely grate the garlic and spread the seasoning in a thin layer.
troubleshooting.fix: Reduce the air fryer to 180°C (356°F) and continue cooking until the thickest part reaches 63°C (145°F).

chef_notes: Fillet thickness affects cooking time more than weight alone; evenly cut center portions are easier to cook consistently.
Drying the surface and leaving space around each fillet encourage light browning.
Lemon zest supplies citrus aroma during cooking, while the juice added afterward keeps the finish bright.
Leaving the fillets in place during cooking helps preserve their shape and delicate flakes.
data.cultural_context: This recipe reflects contemporary American home cooking, using an air fryer for a quick salmon lunch. Lemon, garlic and black pepper provide a familiar seafood seasoning combination that suits the fish's richness.
